_source: design/08 §1.2's table, enforced by tools/size-budget.mjs (the artifact lines) and tools/treeshake-check.mjs (the min+gz lines). Every number is BYTES, because a budget expressed in 'KB' is a budget nobody can diff; 1 KB = 1024 B, the unit §1.2 uses. Changing any line here is a reviewed act with the reason in the commit message and, where the new value is looser than design's, an entry in `_overDesign` — which `size-budget.mjs` and `treeshake-check.mjs` both enforce mechanically (the same rule bench/runtime/budget.json applies to the perf gates, R9).

_design._why: design/08 §1.2's own column, printed beside the measurement on every run so drift from the design document is visible even inside budget.

design/08 §1.2 budgets the kit at ≤ 8 MB unpacked (hard fail 12 MB) and its single bundle file at ≤ 2 MB. There is no bundle line here because there is no bundle: §3.1 bundles the kit with esbuild because CLI cold-start matters, and the CLI does not exist yet (no `bin`, no `src/cli.ts`). The kit ships unbundled `tsc` output with `pg` as a real runtime dependency, so the 2 MB bundle line is not applicable rather than passing — see the AS BUILT note under design/08 §3.1.

design/08 §1.1's table budgets the scaffolder at ≤ 500 KB unpacked, and design/13 decision 7 keeps it at zero dependencies — `node:readline/promises` for the four questions, no prompt library and no chalk. The tarball is `dist/` plus `dist/templates/`, which is the getting-started project as files; nothing here is bundled, so this number moves only when a template does.

design/08 §1.1's table budgets @pg-prime/testing at ≤ 300 KB unpacked and design/13 decision 4 repeats it, so the budget IS design's number — the same shape as the two entries above, where `unpackedBytes` is design/08 §1.2's own column and the measurement is printed beside it on every run. MEASURED 2026-08-30 at the first build (design/13 §3 T): 113 623 B unpacked in 31 files, 63% below design; 43 KB of that is .d.ts and .js and the rest is source maps. It is deliberately NOT ratcheted to the measurement the way the treeshake lines are: those are MINIFIED, so a 1 KB step is real headroom, whereas this line counts the comments tsc keeps — this package is about half docblock by line — and a budget 41 bytes above the measurement would turn a paragraph edit into a red CI job without telling anyone anything. The number to watch is the one the log prints.

packages/pg-prime-testing._whyPeers: design/13 decision 3. Zero runtime `dependencies` — the assertion `zeroDependencies` switches on — with `pg-prime` the one REQUIRED peer (it is the package this one exists to test, and the real-server fixtures talk to the admin database through it rather than shipping a second wire client) and the two fixtures' backends OPTIONAL, each behind a lazy `import()` that fails with a sentence naming it. `size-budget.mjs` fails on any peer not named here, in either list, which is what keeps an optional peer from quietly becoming required.

treeshake._why: design/08 §1.2's min+gz lines, measured by §2.4's method: gzip(esbuild --bundle --format=esm --minify --platform=node) of fixtures/treeshake/<case>/entry.ts resolved THROUGH the package's export map, with rollup + @rollup/plugin-node-resolve run beside it as the independent DCE second opinion. §1.2 says these are provisional and get baselined on the first measurement, then ratcheted downward only.
treeshake._baselined: provisional, baselined 2026-08-28; re-baselined 2026-08-28 for design/11 §3 K2a; re-baselined 2026-08-29 for design/12 §3 B (the six builder gaps: +1 830 / +1 834 / +1 890 B) and for design/12 §3 S (the session layer of design/07 — handles, transactions, the error hierarchy, pooler profiles, observability, LISTEN and COPY: +22 579 B on the connect fixture); and design/12 §3 K4 (`pull`, checkpoints, seeding and the DSL they need — one module and +1 153 B on `root-import-all`); the numbers below are the MERGED round-A tree (B + S + K4 together, measured at the integration on 2026-08-29), not any branch alone. The rule is unchanged — budget = ceil(measured / 1024) * 1024, ratcheting down from there — and `root-import-all` is still 38% BELOW design/08 §1.2 while the two `connect` fixtures are over it and say why in `_overDesign`. The module-set goldens gained 19 entries, which is what design §2.4 step 3 wants a reviewer to see; `pg` is NOT among them, which is design/12 §1 decision 2 s gate.; re-baselined 2026-09-01 for design/14 §G (the DDL close-out: +1 101 / +1 092 / +2 275 B min+gz, module sets unchanged)
treeshake._rule: budget = min(design, ceil(measured / 1024) * 1024). Rounding the measurement up to the next whole KB and never above design's number ratchets three of the four cases BELOW design on their first measurement, and leaves ~2% of headroom so that a comment edit in packages/pg-prime/src does not turn the package job red. The zero-tolerance regression detector for these fixtures is not the byte count — it is fixtures/treeshake/<case>/expected-modules.json, the exact set of modules that contributed bytes, which is what design §2.4 step 3 says actually works.

_measured._when: 2026-09-01, the design/14 merged tree (G + V + W together, measured at integration) — not any branch alone.

_measuredBeforeViews._when: 2026-08-29 (design/12 §4 F1, over the P tree). Kept so design/14 W reads as +867 / +877 / +2 190 B min+gz rather than as an absolute.

_measuredBeforeF1._when: 2026-08-29 (design/12 §4 P items 0 and 2, over the round-A integration). Kept so F1 reads as +864 / +885 / +905 B min+gz rather than as an absolute.

_measuredBeforePerfPass._when: 2026-08-29 (design/12 round-A integration: C + B + S + K4 merged). Kept so design/12 §4 P item 0 reads as +346 / +341 / +344 B min+gz rather than as an absolute.

_measuredBeforeK2a._when: 2026-08-28, the packaging pass (a5f4f9a). Kept so the K2a delta reads as +921 / +911 / +1656 B min+gz rather than as an absolute.

_measuredBeforeSessionLayer._when: 2026-08-28 (design/11 §3 K2a), esbuild 0.28.2, node 24.14.1, packages/pg-prime built with typescript 7.0.2

_measuredBeforeG14._when: 2026-08-29 (design/12 §4 F1), the measurement this line carried until design/14 §G. Kept so G's DDL close-out reads as +1 101 / +1 092 / +2 275 B min+gz.

_measuredBeforeExtensionTypes._when: 2026-08-29 (design/12 §4 F1). Kept so design/14 V reads as +1 328 / +1 330 / +1 762 B min+gz rather than as an absolute.

_overDesign._why: Every entry is a budget deliberately looser than design/08 §1.2's number, with the reason and the measurement. `size-budget.mjs` FAILS on a budget that exceeds its `_design` twin and is not listed here, so widening one is a machine-checkable event and not only a review one. An entry leaves this block by measurement — by the number coming down — never by editing the number.
_overDesign.treeshake.connect-one-select:
design/08 §1.2 budgets 'connect + one select' at 35 KB min+gz. It measured 47 212 B before the session layer and 69 791 B after (+22 579 B, +48%) on the S branch alone; the merged round-A tree (B's builder surface + S) measures 71 560 B, and the budget is baselined at 71 680 B and ratchets down from there.

The delta is exactly design/07 §1.3, and it is STRUCTURAL rather than shaveable: a handle is one object, and `07` §1.3 puts `transaction`, `session`, `listen`, `notify`, `copyFrom`, `copyTo`, `diagnose`, `diagnosePooler`, `observe`, `stats` and `end` ON it. Every one of those is therefore reachable from the first line of any program that calls `pgPrime(...)`, which is the same argument this entry already made about the query builder's `from`/`insertInto`/`update`/`deleteFrom`. The 19 modules the goldens gained are `src/errors/**` (6), `src/session/**` (7), `src/observe/**` (3), `src/pooler/**` (2) and `src/driver/copy.js`; the four largest contributors are `session/handles.js` (13 616 B pre-gzip), `session/runner.js` (10 306 B), `pooler/diagnose.js` (5 545 B) and `errors/classes.js`.

Two things were checked rather than assumed. (1) **`pg` is not in the graph** — decision 2's gate — because `connection:` resolves it through a lazy `import('pg')` in `src/session/pg-lazy.ts` and `pgDriver` is structural. (2) **`node:async_hooks` is not a static import**: the dev guard's `AsyncLocalStorage` is imported inside `transaction()`, and `test/session/session.test.ts`'s module-graph case greps `src/**` to keep it that way.

Making this line meet 35 KB is an API change — a separate `pg-prime/session` entry point, so that `listen`/`copy`/`diagnose` are not members of `Db` — which contradicts `07` §1.3 and is not in this workstream's scope. Recorded in design/07's AS BUILT notes and design/12 §3 S.

design/12 §4 P item 0 adds +346 B min+gz here (71 597 → 71 943, budget 71 680 → 72 704) and +344 B on `root-import-all`. These fixtures are MINIFIED, so none of it is the comments the `jsBytes` note is about: it is the code that took the per-statement fast path apart — the lazy `CompiledStatement` accessors, `captureCallSite`'s structured-frame path plus the string fallback it keeps for runtimes without `prepareStackTrace`, and the option builders and frozen sentinels that replaced four conditional spreads. The module set is UNCHANGED, which is the golden design/08 §2.4 step 3 actually cares about.

design/12 §4 F1 adds +864 / +885 / +905 B min+gz (72 119 -> 72 983 · 72 349 -> 73 234 · 79 235 -> 80 140; budgets 72 704 -> 73 728 and 79 872 -> 80 896). Minified, so again none of it is comments: it is `07` §6.1/§6.2's four option setters on five builder classes and the prepared artifact, the `run` field on five state records, and the client-side `$default`/`$onUpdate` application in `query/meta.ts` / `insert.ts` / `update.ts`. **The module set is unchanged**, and keeping it that way was a deliberate edit: `withRunOption` started life in `src/query/builder-state.ts`, which is types-only at runtime, and one exported value there put `builder-state.js` into all three bundles (+305 B on `connect-one-select`, and three `expected-modules.json` diffs). It lives in `./terminals.ts` instead, which is already in every graph.

+1 101 B by design/14 §G (73 728 -> 74 752, measured 74 084). `schema/extras.js` is NOT in this fixture's module set, so `exclude()` and the index-option builders cost it nothing; what it does pay for is three files it already pulled — `schema/column.js` (the `.generatedAlwaysAs()` method and its four declaration-time refusals), `schema/table.js` (`pgTable`'s names-only pre-pass for the `(cols) => fragment` form, which is guarded by a scan that exits on the first column and returns `undefined` for every schema that uses none) and `query/meta.js` + `session/copy.js` (`generatedKeys`, and the `42P10` sentence COPY now says itself). A good part of it is the message TEXT: esbuild strips comments and keeps strings, so an error sentence is the one kind of prose a user's bundle really carries. The trade is the one design/13 §5's F3 note already took — a `23502` or a `42P10` arriving from the server with no column name in it costs more than 1 KB.

design/14 W (design/01 §3 row 58, views) adds +867 / +877 / +2 190 B min+gz (72 983 -> 73 850 · 73 234 -> 74 111 · 80 140 -> 82 330; budgets 73 728 -> 74 752 and 80 896 -> 82 944). design/14 V (extension types) re-baselines 73 728 -> 74 752 B; measured 74 311 B, +1 328 min+gz, ceil-to-1 KB. The module set gained exactly two entries in all three fixtures — `codec/define.js` and `codec/extensions.js` — and they are UNAVOIDABLE on this path rather than a missed shake: `Registry`'s constructor registers the `citext` and `vector` codecs by name so that `t.citext()` and `t.vector(n)` resolve through `codecFor`'s ordinary scalar path (design/14 decision 5), and `connect + one select` builds a `Registry`. The alternative — leaving them to the caller to register — trades 1.3 KB for an API where the shipped extension types do not work out of the box, which is not the trade design/01 §3 row 62 asks for. `full-crud-tx` moved +1 330 B and `root-import-all` +1 762 B (the latter is still 33 % BELOW design and needs no entry here).
_overDesign.packages/pg-prime.largestDtsBytes:
design/08 §1.2's canary is 40 KB per declaration file; `dist/query/types.d.ts` measured 54 843 B before design/12 round A, 62 502 B with S alone, 64 531 B with B alone, and 72 190 B on the merged tree; the budget is set AT the merged measurement so any growth at all fails CI and needs a visible diff. B's +9 688 B is the declaration cost of the six builder gaps (`$all` and its `AllRefs` carrier on four scope types, `avg`/`min`/`max` on `RelAggs`, six join signatures plus the two laterals, `withRecursive` and `fromRaw` on both executors, `RecursiveOpts`/`FromRawOpts`/`RawShape` — every one a documented name in tools/api-snapshot/pg-prime.json). S's +7 632 B is design/07 §1.3's four handle interfaces — `Queryable`, `Db`, `Tx`, `Session` — which have to live in this file because they are what the query builder's own entry points hang off; the session layer's other ~40 types are in `src/session/types.d.ts` (5.9 KB) precisely so that they do not land here. Splitting `query/types.ts` is still the PUBLIC-API refactor the previous note describes and is still out of scope. Design's 40 960 stays in `_design` and is printed beside the measurement on every run.

design/12 §4 F1 re-baselines 72 190 -> 76 358 B (+4 168, the budget again set AT the measurement). All of it is `07` §6.1/§6.2's builder-level option methods, which S recorded as not done because `Query` was another workstream's file: `.signal()`, `.timeout()`, `.outsideTransaction()` and `.withExecMode()` on six interfaces — `Query`, `GroupedQuery`, `SetQuery`, `InsertQuery`, `UpdateQuery`, `DeleteQuery` — at 24 method signatures plus their JSDoc. They are written out inline rather than behind one generic `QueryOptionMethods<Self>` mixin ON PURPOSE: a self-parameterised interface would be a fresh instantiation per `Query<S, O, N>` on the hot type path this file exists to keep cheap, and `bench:types` is the gate that would have to pay for it. Measured: the headline instantiation counts did not move (see design/12 §4 F1 — RESULT).

Re-baselined 76 358 -> 78 393 B by design/14 W (design/01 §3 row 58, views), the budget again set AT the measurement. +2 035 B, and it is the read-only guard rather than the view types: `insertInto` / `update` / `deleteFrom` on BOTH `Executor` and `CteExecutor` become return-position sentinels — six signatures whose bodies each spell `OrmTypeError<WriteToViewMsg<…>>` INLINE, which `src/query/errors.ts`'s header explains is mandatory (a named alias prints unexpanded and defeats the whole mechanism) — plus `Queryable.refreshMaterializedView` and its docblock. The view TYPES are not in this file at all: `View`, `MaterializedView`, `ViewTable`, `ViewSchema` and the two builder stages live in `dist/schema/view.d.ts` (13.0 KB), a new file well under the 40 KB canary. Splitting `query/types.ts` is still the public-API refactor the notes above describe and is still out of scope.

_overDesign.packages/pg-prime.jsBytes:
design/08 §1.2 budgets 700 KB of shipped .js and the package measures 889 072 B (868.2 KB) on the merged round-A tree (852 713 B with S alone; K4's DSL additions — `pgDomain`/`pgSequence`/`pgExtension`, the index options, `partitionBy`/`partitionOf`, `clusterOn`, `t.raw` — are the last +11.5 KB), 29% over — the package measures 902 697 B on the tree with design/12 §4 P merged (P's `statement-path` gate and the encode-path rewrite) and the budget is 903 168 B by the same rule; before that 889 856 B and then 890 880 B after the one-time `oxfmt` pass (design/12 decision 19) added 1 689 B of emitted line structure — tsc keeps comments and line breaks, so a formatter moves this number; the ceil-to-1 KB rule leaves less than 1 KB of margin by construction and that is the point of it (a diff to this file is the reviewed act). Current budget — the same `ceil(measured / 1024) * 1024` rounding the treeshake lines use, so it ratchets down from here. The whole of the increase is design/07's session layer, which did not exist when the number was written: `src/session/` (the handles, the two runners, transactions and savepoints, the retry loop, the dev guard, LISTEN, COPY encoding, the GUC policy), `src/errors/` (the ~50-class §4.2 tree, the SQLSTATE table as data, redaction, constraint resolution), `src/pooler/` (the profiles and the two diagnostics) and `src/observe/` (hooks, the OTel mapping, the slow-query log) — about 88 KB of source that design/08 §1.2's 700 KB predates by one workstream. What it costs a USER is the treeshake line, and that is measured too: `connect-one-select` moved +22 579 B min+gz, because `07` §1.3 puts every session method ON the handle — see `treeshake.connect-one-select` in this block for the module-by-module account. Recorded in design/07's AS BUILT notes and design/12 §3 S RESULT.

Re-baselined 890 880 → 898 048 B by design/12 §4 P item 0. The pass removed work from the per-statement fast path and ADDED 7.0 KB of shipped .js doing it, which is worth stating plainly: ~3 KB is code (`CompiledStatement` as a class with three lazy accessors, `captureCallSite`'s structured-frame path plus its string fallback, `runOptionsFor`, `acquireOptions`, `observed`, the frozen sentinels) and ~4 KB is the comments that say why — tsc keeps comments, so in this package prose is shipped bytes and a perf finding recorded in the code costs the user something. The trade was taken once, deliberately, and the comments were cut by ~40 % first; the account that does NOT fit in the source lives in design/12 §4 P — RESULT. This line is a size budget, not a prose budget, and it ratchets down from here like the others. Then 898 048 -> 902 144 for item 2, the batch-insert encode path: the rewritten `#valuesSource`, the `$n` table in the emitter and the indexed row-key check, plus their measurements — 3.6 KB for a compile that went 1 680 -> 631 µs on a 1 000-row insert.
